name: AlbEmo
full_title: AlbEmo: an emotional speech corpus for Albanian
license_note: Zenodo record 21638085 (AlbEmo v1.0, 2026-07-28): CC BY 4.0 (Zenodo API re-read 2026-10-26; the archive also has a LICENSE file); checked by the maintainer [albemo_page].
notes: AlbEmo (University of Tirana), first emotional speech corpus for Albanian [albemo_page]; Zenodo 21638085, 92 MB [albemo_page]. Ten native Albanian speakers (5 female, 5 male; aged 18 to over 55) recorded six semantically neutral sentences in seven styles (Ekman's six emotions and neutral): 420 recordings, 48 kHz 16-bit mono, 22.1 min (0.3679 h), clips 1.2-10.1 s [albemo_page]. Recorded alone in a quiet office with a USB cardioid microphone and a purpose-built offline browser tool, with browser-side processing disabled [albemo_page]. Folder names are Albanian emotion words [albemo_page]. Listening test: 4 evaluators, 1,260 judgements; in the review's recount 918 judgements are correct; the majority differs from the intention for 63 clips and no evaluator got 31 clips right (disgust 15) [albemo_page]. The scripts/, tools/ and README mentioned in the description are not in the downloaded archive (the record lists them) [albemo_page].

Folders 01Neutral to 05Angry; file name xn-yy-aa-gg-bb (emotion code, sentence 01-07, repetition, gender code, speaker) [ased_page]. Sentences 03-07 are the emotion-specific ones (all-or-nothing per speaker: 37 speakers have all 50, 28 have none, per the review) [ased_page].

Labelled by listeners with a vote (5 annotators for the first 52 folders, 3 others for later ones) [asvpesd_page]. File-name fields vary between 8 and 12 and hold values (language, source, intensity) that the description does not explain [asvpesd_page].

notes: Alibaba AIDC-AI (named ATH-MaaS on Hugging Face) [csemotions_paper]. Released with the Marco-Voice technical report (arXiv 2508.02038) [csemotions_card_2]. The card's column names (transcript / speaker_id / gender / prompt_id) differ from the actual columns (audio / text / emotion / speaker) [csemotions_paper]. The paper says each speaker read 100 Chinese and English prompts, but the data has 1,296 distinct Chinese sentences [csemotions_card_2]. The paper's evaluation prompts are 100 per emotion (English and Chinese) [csemotions_card_2]. The 1,296 sentences (`text` column) are each read in one emotion only: none occurs in more than one emotion (checked by exact match). [csemotions_readme]

The paper counts dialogues with added fillers (uh, um) as 962 for speaker 0 and 689 for speaker 1 (the release does not mark which) [dailytalk_paper_2]. The paper says dialogues with more than 5 turns were selected, but the shortest dialogue in the data has 5 utterances [dailytalk_paper_2]. The release also keeps the turn order, topic and dialogue act of every utterance (`metadata.json`). [dailytalk_readme]

name: EMIS
full_title: Emotionally Incongruent Synthetic Speech Dataset
license_note: Zenodo record license: GPL-3.0-or-later (checked by the maintainer, 2026-10-24) [emis_page]. The audio was synthesised from ESD reference voices by three TTS systems; the record and the paper do not discuss their terms [emis_paper]. Read on 2026-10-24: ESD has an MIT LICENSE file, but its README asks users to sign a license form and says the database can only be used for research purpose [emis_paper]. CosyVoice2 code and model are Apache-2.0 on the model card, but its paper says the training data came from internal tools and does not name the sources [emis_paper]. StyleTTS2 code is MIT; its README asks users of the pre-trained models to tell listeners that speech is synthesised unless the voice owner permitted it [emis_paper]. Which checkpoints EMIS used, and how model terms reach generated audio, is not stated [emis_paper]. Whether GPL-3.0-or-later overrides these conditions is not stated either [emis_paper].
notes: Corrêa, Lima, Moreno, Ueda, Costa (UNICAMP) [emis_page]. Paper: arXiv 2510.25054 (Zenodo links the ICASSP 2026 DOI 10.1109/ICASSP55912.2026.11462441, whose text was not seen) [emis_page]. Synthetic speech [emis_page]. 104 emotion-rich sentences written by GPT-4.5 (the Zenodo record says ChatGPT-4.5): per emotion (angry, happy, sad) explicit and implicit sentences, plus neutral sentences; each was synthesised in four voice emotions (angry, happy, neutral, sad) by F5-TTS, CosyVoice2 and StyleTTS2 (named in the paper; file names say F5TTS, COSY, STYLE) [emis_page]. Reference audio: for each generation one of the 10 ESD English speakers (0011-0020) was drawn at random and their 7 longest utterances concatenated (about 30 s) [emis_paper]. F5TTS files are PCM_16 and the others float [emis_page]. 936 files have a voice emotion different from the text emotion and 312 are congruent [emis_page]. 26 sentence groups (number at the start of the file name): groups 01-13 hold six emotional sentences and one neutral sentence, groups 14-26 one neutral sentence each [emis_paper].

name: EmoNet-Voice
full_title: EmoNet-Voice: A Fine-Grained, Expert-Verified Benchmark for Speech Emotion Detection
language_note: 4 languages (paper abstract; the languages are not named there) [emonetvoice_paper]
license_note: The card of the Hugging Face repository holding Bench (an anonymous review account, t1a5anu-anon) says CC BY 4.0 [emonetvoice_paper].
notes: Schuhmann et al. (LAION, 2025) [emonetvoice_paper]. EmoNet-Voice Big is synthetic speech for pre-training (the abstract says 5,000 hours; the per-language sum in Table 2 is 4,752 hours [emonetvoice_paper]; Table 1 says >1M items and >4,500 hours) [emonetvoice_paper]. EmoNet-Voice Bench is an evaluation set of 12,600 items (36.26 hours) chosen from Big [emonetvoice_paper]; 6 experts (psychology bachelor or higher) gave 33,605 ratings (2-4 per item) [emonetvoice_paper]. The abstract's 4.7k is the unanimous part [emonetvoice_paper]. Inter-rater Cronbach's alpha is 0.14 [emonetvoice_paper]. It includes, through synthesis, emotions that are hard to collect from people, such as pain and shame [emonetvoice_paper]. Distributed through the paper's Hugging Face collection laion/emonet: emonet-voice-bench (12,600 items, CC-BY-4.0) and emonet-voice-foundation under the anonymous account t1a5anu-anon [emonetvoice_paper]. The foundation card points to laion/laions_got_talent_enhanced_flash_annotations_and_long_captions as the main data [emonetvoice_paper]. The paper says it is released as a research artefact for academic use [emonetvoice_paper].

name: EmoSpeech (keyword)
license_note: Kaggle license field: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 [emospeech_keywords_page]. The bundled License.txt is Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International, and the paper says the data is released for non-commercial purposes (checked by the maintainer, 2026-10-24) [emospeech_keywords_paper].
notes: Indian EmoSpeech Command Dataset (Banga, Upadhyay, Agarwal, Sharma, Mukherjee, arXiv 1910.13801, 2019) [emospeech_keywords_paper]. Kaggle ujjwal9/emospeech (free account) [emospeech_keywords_page]. 3-second commands recorded on phones in real surroundings (house, metro, roads, railway, near a lake, ...), each with a keyword, an emotion and an environment sound [emospeech_keywords_paper]. Keyword classes: help, bachao (spelled bacho in the files), stop, go, yes, no, `unknown` (any other word) and `background` (sound whose source is not human vocal chords, e.g. birds or road noise; paper Section 5) [emospeech_keywords_paper]. Emotions: calm, happy, angry, fearful, and a tag None [emospeech_keywords_page]. Environment tag in the file name: safe, scream, glass break, gunshots (the README does not list scream) [emospeech_keywords_paper]. Collection: Android app, then a game-like web app [emospeech_keywords_paper]; 250 speakers (paper); privacy-policy consent [emospeech_keywords_paper]. Quality control: samples whose word reviewers cannot tell are rejected, each sample is checked by two people, and emotion is matched against reference samples (Section 4.4) [emospeech_keywords_paper]. The hash field has 103 values and does not match the paper's 250 speakers [emospeech_keywords_paper]. Language is not stated (English and Hindi words) [emospeech_keywords_paper].

Each clip has 3-5 human emotion captions, an emotion label and a transcript [emospeech_secap_paper]. Split: test 600, validation 600, train 29,326 sentences; only test is public (dataset/ on GitHub: wav.scp, text.txt, fid2captions.json) [emospeech_secap_paper].

name: EmoTale
full_title: EmoTale: An Enacted Speech-emotion Dataset in Danish
license_note: The repository (snehadas/EmoTale, commit 41e7d00f) has no LICENSE file and GitHub shows no license [emotale_paper]. The datasheet answers 'Will the dataset be distributed under a copyright or other IP license?' with: 'The data will be distributed under a copyright [emotale_datasheet]. There is no license, but there is a request to cite the corresponding paper if the dataset is used.' The project treats the request to cite the paper as the terms of use (the maintainer's decision, 2026-10-26), as for IESC, so the class is open [emotale_paper].
notes: Hjuler, Skat-Rørdam, Clemmensen, Das (DTU, ASRU 2025, arXiv 2508.14548; collected as part of a master's thesis) [emotale_paper]. Enacted speech in Danish and English [emotale_datasheet]. Participants with acting experience were recruited (age at least 7, Danish speakers); recorded in quiet rooms with wireless Rode microphones at 48 kHz (stereo 16-bit wav in the release) [emotale_paper]. 18 participants (12 female, 6 male, 9-39 years, mean 22.8 [emotale_paper]; 3 are children aged 9-12) enacted 5 emotionally neutral sentences (translated from Emo-DB) in 5 emotions (anger, happiness, sadness, boredom, neutral), self-inducing the emotion by recalling a situation; only the last take was kept [emotale_paper]. File names: language_speaker_emotion_sentence (e.g [emotale_page]. DK_004_A_5.wav) [emotale_datasheet]. Written consent under GDPR, IRB approval (documents in the repository) [emotale_datasheet]. The label is the enacted emotion; annotations.csv additionally holds three annotators' perceived categories and arousal-valence-dominance ratings (the annotators are three authors of the paper) [emotale_paper]. The README says two annotators; the paper reports agreement between annotators 1 and 2 and the file holds three [emotale_paper]. The datasheet warns that the dataset is small and not suited for tasks needing large-scale training or natural emotional speech [emotale_paper].

notes: Sun et al. (Nankai University and BAAI, arXiv 2505.23018, 2025) [emotiontalk_paper]. Two-person dialogues by 19 professional actors [emotiontalk_paper]. Audio, video and text [emotiontalk_paper]. Hugging Face holds WebDataset tar files [emotiontalk_paper]. The Hugging Face page counts (neutral 6,853 and so on) are those of the audio+video (multimodal) labels, not of the audio labels [emotiontalk_paper]. Audio-label counts (recipe, json audio field; paper section 3.3 agrees): neutral 9,378 / angry 3,820 / happy 2,105 / surprised 1,363 / sad 1,110 / disgusted 818 / fearful 656 [emotiontalk_paper]. 6,647 utterances are marked as overlapping speech [emotiontalk_paper]. full_title: EMOVO Corpus: an Italian Emotional Speech Database
notes: Costantini et al., LREC 2014 [emovo_paper]. Six actors (3 male, 3 female) x 14 sentences x 7 emotions = 588 files, 0.51 h [emovo_paper]; A listening test on two sentences gave 80% overall accuracy [emovo_paper].

name: EmoVoice-DB
license_note: All audio is synthesised with OpenAI's GPT-4o-audio [emovoicedb_paper]. Which terms applied to the API use when EmoVoice-DB was made (early 2025), and whether training a speech emotion recognizer counts under these terms, is not stated in any source read [emovoicedb_paper]. The card and the paper do not mention OpenAI's terms [emovoicedb_paper].
notes: Yang et al. (EmoVoice, arXiv 2504.12867, ACM MM 2025) [emovoicedb_paper]. English synthetic emotional speech; every clip generated by GPT-4o-audio [emovoicedb_paper]. Steps (card and paper): (1) GPT-4o writes pairs of text (novel excerpts, dialogue, observations) and emotion description; (2) GPT-4o-audio is prompted with text and description (e.g. 'Repeat this sentence with the emotion of <description>: <text>') in one of 5 voices (ash, ballad, coral, sage, verse); (3) samples with high WER are removed; (4) GPT-4o rephrases each description twice, giving three descriptions per sample in train [emovoicedb_paper]. 7 emotions: angry, happy, sad, surprised, disgusted, fearful, neutral [emovoicedb_paper]. The five voices are synthetic timbres, not people [emovoicedb_paper]. The card's text example for test.jsonl includes a neutral prompt speech file [emovoicedb_paper].

Harper Valley Bank
full_title: Harper Valley Bank Spoken Dialog Corpus
license_note: The repository's `LICENSE` is the full text of Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International. "How to Cite" in the README gives the BibTeX of arXiv:2010.13929 [arxiv_s_2010_13929].
notes: Wu, Nafziger, Scodary, Maas (Gridspace and Stanford) [arxiv_s_2010_13929]. 1,446 simulated call-centre calls, 59 speakers (in agent and caller roles) [arxiv_s_2010_13929]. One call = 2 wav files (one per side, 8 kHz mono PCM_16) [arxiv_s_2010_13929]. Human transcripts by trained Gridspace Mixer workers [arxiv_s_2010_13929]. Segmentation follows the word times of Gridspace's automatic speech recognition (paper: "automatic segmentation") [harper_valley_bank_page]. In all 25,730 segments `duration_ms` matches the end of the last word of the machine transcript [harper_valley_bank_page]. The corpus has no speaker gender, age or other attributes [arxiv_s_2010_13929]. Simulated calls (crowd workers phoning from scripts), with vocabulary limited to about 700 words: scripted, acted conversation rather than real customers' emotions [arxiv_s_2010_13929]. Labels are the output of Gridspace's automatic model, not human, and no human verification is described (neither the paper nor the README gives the model's name, version, training data or accuracy) [harper_valley_bank_page]. Setting: human-agent interaction [arxiv_s_2010_13929].

name: JVNV

notes: JVNV (Xin et al.), arXiv 2310.06072: 4 professional Japanese speakers, about 4 hours (3.94 h used), 48 kHz, anechoic room, up to 4 hours per speaker [jvnv_paper]. Each utterance contains at least one nonverbal vocalisation (laughter, crying, etc.) [jvnv_paper]. Sessions: regular (the nonverbal phrase is specified, 1,375 clips) and free (the speaker chooses the phrase, 240 clips) [jvnv_page]. Scripts were generated with ChatGPT (gpt-3.5-turbo-0301) in a way that balances phonemes [jvnv_paper]. A listening test (crowd, forced choice) gave 94.21% (87.37% without the nonverbal parts). transcription.csv has 514 rows; nv_label/ has the nonverbal intervals of 1,615 files (neither used by the recipe) [jvnv_paper].

name: A Kannada Emotional Speech Dataset

Includes child speakers (two aged 12 and one aged 17) [kannada_page]. The train and test counts of paper Table 7 (emotions per split) do not match the measurements [nonverbaltts_paper]. The VoxCeleb part is in-the-wild YouTube audio, an evaluation set close to YODAS, worth looking at separately [nonverbaltts_paper]. The Expresso part is read and improvised dialogue of a different nature [nonverbaltts_paper]. Emotion labels are automatic classification plus annotator review; their reliability needs checking [nonverbaltts_paper]. The clips come from two sources, separable by the `data_name` column: VoxCeleb 4,452 clips (13.68 hours, 16 kHz) and Expresso 1,804 clips (3.91 hours, 48 kHz). [nonverbaltts_readme]

name: USC-EMO-MRI
full_title: USC-EMO-MRI: An emotional speech production database
license_note: Zenodo license field: CC BY 4.0 (deposited on Zenodo 2026-03-30) [usc_emo_mri_page]. CC BY 4.0 requires attribution; the citation from Zenodo is used (as specified by the maintainer, 2026-10-19): Kim, J., Toutios, A., Kim, Y.-C., Zhu, Y., Lee, S., & Narayanan, S. (2014) [usc_emo_mri_page]. USC-EMO-MRI: An emotional speech production database [Dataset] [usc_emo_mri_page]. 10th International Seminar on Speech Production (ISSP) [usc_emo_mri_page]. USC-EMO-MRI corpus: An emotional speech production database recorded by real-time magnetic resonance imaging, Cologne, Germany. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19325044 [usc_emo_mri_page].
notes: Kim, Toutios, Lee, Narayanan (USC SAIL) [usc_emo_mri_page]. 5 men and 5 women with professional acting experience lay supine in an MRI scanner and read English sentences (6 sentences + repeated utterances for some speakers + the Grandfather passage) in 4 target emotions [usc_emo_mri_paper_2]. The MRI captures the mid-sagittal plane of the vocal tract at 23.18 frames/s and 68x68 pixels; audio was recorded simultaneously at 20 kHz and denoised afterwards with adaptive signal processing (paper §2.2) [usc_emo_mri_paper_2]. Fast speaking rate only for neutral (98 utterances) [usc_emo_mri_paper_2]. The archive is AVI (video + audio); there are no wav files [usc_emo_mri_paper_2]. Labels are the majority vote of the emotion perceived by 10-12 listeners (paper §2.3; listeners per speaker in Table 2); agreement with the target emotion ranges from 69.5% (M2) to 94.0% (F2) as speaker means [usc_emo_mri_paper_2]. Per-rater choices, confidence and strength, and the performers' target emotions, are not in the archive (the paper's Data availability says "the emotion evaluation result of each utterance" is public) [usc_emo_mri_paper_2]. Speech acted inside an MRI scanner, not a corpus built for speech emotion recognition (the paper studies the articulation of emotional expression) [usc_emo_mri_paper_2]. The remaining noise level was not measured [usc_emo_mri_paper_2]. Labels are the listeners' majority vote and some differ from the performers' intention [usc_emo_mri_paper_2]. The recipe's valid set is a single speaker (f2) [usc_emo_mri_paper_2].
